newsitem.title: CHINA: China to expand foreign insurers, investment banks.
newsitem.headline: China to expand foreign insurers, investment banks.

text.p: China will expand the number of foreign insurance firms and investment banks allowed to operate in the country this year, the China Securities quoted central bank governor Dai Xianglong as saying.
"China will continue to expand the opening of its finance industry to foreigners," the newspaper quoted Dai, head of the People's Bank of China, as saying recently.

Based on the experience of allowing foreign banks to conduct domestic yuan currency business in Shanghai's Pudong district, the bank will make preparations to expand the scope of the pilot scheme in the future, the newspaper said.
The bank would gradually expand the number of foreign insurers and investment banks in China, it quoted Dai as saying.

The central bank would also decide on the regional distribution as well as the number of foreign financial organisations and boost cooperation with foreign banking supervisory organisations and the Bank for International Settlement.

At the end of March, 158 foreign banks had offices in China, of which 132 had branches, the newspaper said. At end-1996, the assets of foreign financial institutions in China had risen to $30 billion, up 56.3 percent compared with the year-ago period, it said.
